thread.title: Tiffany Holiday Q4 Earnings Shine But Same-Store Sales Hit Stock |

author: ELAINE LOW
title: Tiffany Holiday Q4 Earnings Shine But Same-Store Sales Hit Stock |
text:
Tiffany ( TIF ) had a sparkling holiday fourth quarter, with the higher-end jeweler reporting strong earnings early Friday and offering upbeat guidance. But same-store sales growth came in below views. Shares fell in early trading in the stock market today .
X Estimates : Per-share profit of $1.63, up 12%, on 6% sales growth to $1.305 billion, according to Zacks Investment Research. Same-store sales were expected to rise 4.7%, or 2.7% on a constant currency basis.
Results : EPS of $1.67 on revenue of $1.334 billion, up 8.5%. Global same-store sales rose 3%, or 1% on a constant-currency basis. Comps grew 4% in the Americas, were flat in Japan and down 8% in Europe.
Outlook : Tiffany sees current-year earnings of $4.25-$4.45, vs. the consensus for $4.25. Sales should rise in the midsingle digits. Analysts expect full-year revenue of $4.344 billion, a 4% rise.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Stock : Shares fell 5.1% to 97.50, closing above their 200-day line after undercutting their level intraday. Heading into earnings, Tiffany shares had been struggling to retake support at their 50-day moving average, trading below the key level for most of February and all of March thus far. Signet ( SIG ), operator of several mall-based mass-market jewelry chains, was up 3.1%.
IBD'S TAKE: Buying or holding a stock can be risky heading into an earnings report. Here's an earnings options strategy that can help you cash in on post-earnings stock gains, while minimizing the risk from a weak quarter. 
Tiffany had already pre-announced that sales for the two months ended Dec. 31 increased 8% to $1.05 billion with same-store sales up 5%.
Signet, which is more mall-based via its Kay and Jared chains, topped quarterly earnings views on Wednesday but forecast full-year EPS of $3.75-$4.25, well below consensus views for $6.08, on revenue of $5.9 billion-$6.1 billion, below the consensus for $6.18 billion.
Signet has hardly closed a day above its 50-day since last November, and weak guidance had investors punishing the stock again on Wednesday.
